Assume the beam is isotropic, homogeneous, and linear-elastic.
Assume small deformations and that plane sections remain plane.
Assume pure bending about a principal axis of the rectangular cross-section.
Assume no axial force, no torsion, and no transverse shear contribution to bending stress.
Let x be the beam axis, z the width direction, and y the thickness direction measured from the neutral axis.
Let the applied internal bending moment be M acting about the z-axis.
Let the rectangular cross-section have width b and height h.
Let I be the second moment of area of the cross-section about the z-axis, I = b h^3 / 12.
The bending stress at an arbitrary fiber located at distance y from the neutral axis is sigma_x(y) = - M y / I.
The bending stress varies linearly through the beam thickness.
The bending stress is zero at the neutral axis.
The maximum bending stress magnitude occurs at the outermost fibers, y = +h/2 or y = -h/2, and has magnitude sigma_max = 6 M / (b h^2).
The longitudinal strain at the same fiber is epsilon_x(y) = sigma_x(y) / E.
The curvature of the beam under the applied moment is kappa = M / (E I).
The relevant response quantities are the bending stress distribution, the maximum bending stress, the strain distribution, and the curvature.
